description: The three pulse voices of the General Instrument AY-3-8910, with the chip's shared noise generator and looping envelope

params.text: Sets the pitch of that pulse, five octaves either side of C4
Sets the rate of the shared envelope generator, from a fraction of a hertz to several hundred hertz
Attenuates the voltage at that pulse's MOD jack before it is added to the pitch, and inverts it below zero
Sets the level of that pulse, 0 to 15
Switched on, the pulse tone is mixed into that voice
Switched on, the shared noise is mixed into that voice
Switched on, that voice takes its level from the shared envelope generator instead of its AMP setting
Sets the pitch of the shared noise, 0 to 31, with the highest setting giving the shortest period and so the brightest hiss
Steps the shared envelope through its eight shapes in turn, and the lamp below shows which one by colour

inputs.text: Raises the pitch of that pulse by a volt per octave; unpatched it reads the VOCT jack of the pulse before it, and the first pulse reads 0V
Sets the rate of the shared envelope at a volt per octave; unpatched it reads pulse C's VOCT jack
Modulates the pitch of that pulse, a full octave per 5V with the MOD knob wide open; unpatched it reads the MOD jack of the pulse before it, and the first pulse reads 5V
Scales that pulse's AMP knob by the voltage here, 10V leaving the knob untouched and 0V silencing it; unpatched it reads the AMP jack of the pulse before it, and the first pulse reads 10V
Flips that voice's TONE switch while it is above 2V
Flips that voice's NOISE switch while it is above 2V
Flips that voice's ENV switch while it is above 2V
Moves the shared noise pitch, 7V spanning all thirty-two settings
Restarts that pulse from the beginning of its cycle on each rise past 2V; unpatched it reads the SYNC jack of the pulse before it
Restarts the shared envelope on each rise past 2V; unpatched it reads pulse C's SYNC jack

outputs.text: Carries that pulse's audio, hard clipped at 5V, with the audio of any earlier pulse whose own output is unpatched added in

notes: turning a voice's TONE and NOISE switches both off puts it into the chip's four-bit converter mode: its AMP jack becomes an audio input, its VOCT an offset and its MOD a scaling
the three outputs are chained: a pulse whose output is left unpatched is summed into the next output along, so patching only the third output gives a mix of all three
